cards.text: Last time, David got his family back from the Amalekites (1 Samuel 30:18-19). Now the Philistines are fighting against Israel, and Saul, Israel's king, is right in the middle of it. Pull up a stool, friend.

cards.question: The battle is on Mount Gilboa. How does it go for the men of Israel?

cards.text: The Philistines chase Saul and his sons hard. One of those sons is Jonathan, David's dear friend (1 Samuel 18:1-3).

cards.question: Jonathan, Saul's son, makes it out of the battle alive.

cards.text: Then the battle intensifies, and it's pressing right on Saul himself. I'm holding my breath over here, friend.

cards.question: As the battle gets fierce around Saul, the ___ overtake him and wound him critically.

cards.text: Saul is badly wounded. He turns to his armor-bearer, because he doesn't want the Philistines getting to him first.

cards.question: What does wounded Saul ask his armor-bearer to do?

answers.text: Run him through with his sword

cards.question: Saul's armor-bearer does what Saul asks him to do.

cards.text: Friend, I've got nothing funny for this one. His armor-bearer is terrified and refuses, so Saul takes his own sword and falls on it.

cards.question: When Saul's armor-bearer sees that Saul is dead, what does he do?

answers.text: Falls on his own sword too

cards.text: Saul, his three sons, his armor-bearer and all his men die together that same day. One day, friend, and Israelites in the valley and across the Jordan see it all.

cards.question: The Israelites in the valley and across the Jordan see that the army fled and Saul and his sons are dead. What do they do?

answers.text: Crown a new king right away

cards.question: So the ___ came and moved into the cities those Israelites left behind.

cards.text: The next day, the Philistines come back to strip the dead. And there on Mount Gilboa, they find Saul and his three sons.

cards.question: The Philistines cut off Saul's ___ and strip off his ___.
The Philistines send messengers all over their land to spread the news about Saul. Where do the messengers announce it?

answers.text: In the temples of their idols
In the tents of Israel's army

cards.text: They put Saul's armor in the temple of the Ashtoreths. Then they hang his body on a city wall.

cards.question: The Philistines hang Saul's body on the wall of ___.

cards.text: Word reaches the people of Jabesh-gilead. Years ago, Saul rescued that town from the Ammonites (1 Samuel 11:1-11).

cards.question: When the men of valor of Jabesh-gilead hear what the Philistines did to Saul, what do they do?

answers.text: Travel all night and bring the bodies back
Send word to David in Ziklag
Gather an army to attack Gath

cards.text: All night, friend. I can't make it past the second oven timer without nodding off. They bring the bodies of Saul and his sons to Jabesh and burn them there.

cards.question: The men of Jabesh bury the bones under the ___ tree in Jabesh.
After the burial, the people of Jabesh fast for seven days.

findings.problem: The card cites only 1 Samuel 31:6, but its second sentence tells 31:7 (the Israelites in the valley and across the Jordan seeing what happened). The citation should be 1 Samuel 31:6-7.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "see it all" goes beyond 31:7. The text says only that they saw the army had fled and that Saul and his sons had died. It doesn't say they watched everything happen.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The question says the messengers go "all over their land," meaning Philistine land. That rules out both wrong answers, "In the tents of Israel's army" and "On the walls of Jericho," which are Israelite places. Only the right answer is left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Travel all night and bring the bodies back" (8 words), is clearly longer and more detailed than the wrong answers, "Send word to David in Ziklag" and "Gather an army to attack Gath." That makes it stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences. Only the opening card may have up to 3.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The statement says "the people of Jabesh fast for seven days." In 31:12-13, "they" points back to "all their men of valor," the ones who brought back and buried the bodies. The card should name them the way the text does, or just say "they."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Most of this stop's choice cards are discovery questions with no context the baker can reason from: card 2 (head and armor), card 5 (Beth-shan), card 9 (tamarisk) and card 10 (seven days). Only card 7 is set up for an informed guess. Add context to the story cards or ask different questions.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin opens with "Friend, I've got nothing funny for this one." before telling Saul's death. The line is reverent, but it calls attention to his joking as something he does on purpose. The docs say there is no formula and also that he is FUNNY, but they don't say whether he may openly decline to joke.
findings.question: In a grave moment like a suicide or a death, may Papa Dorin say out loud that he has nothing funny to say, or should he just change his tone without remarking on it?
